cases.statement: If entire functions F_n have only real zeros, F_n converge locally uniformly on C to a nonzero entire function F, then F has only real zeros. Moreover, on a small disk around an isolated zero of F whose boundary is zero-free, Rouche/Hurwitz zero counting transports the total multiplicity for all sufficiently large n.
assumptions: each F_n is entire and has no zeros off the real axis
F_n -> F locally uniformly on C
F is entire and not identically zero
for multiplicity counting, choose a compact disk whose boundary contains no zero of F
cases.conclusion: A source-normalized locally-uniform determinant convergence theorem to the exact nonzero Xi function would be target-side sufficient to exclude nonreal Xi zeros; multiplicity can be controlled compact-by-compact.
cases.limitation: This does not prove the RH approximants converge to Xi, does not supply source-side normalization, and does not establish the finite-stage real-zero hypotheses along a cofinal family.

cases.construction: On l2(N), let P_n be the rank-one orthogonal projection onto e_n and A_n=P_n. Then A_n -> 0 strongly. For every z off the real axis, (A_n-zI)^(-1)=(-1/z)I + (1/(1-z)+1/z)P_n, so A_n -> 0 in strong resolvent sense. Yet 1 is an eigenvalue of every A_n and is absent from the spectrum of the limit 0.
cases.conclusion: Strong-resolvent convergence alone does not preserve every approximant eigenvalue or complete spectral multiset.
cases.limitation: This does not show the specific RH approximants have disappearing spectrum; it rejects strong-resolvent convergence as a generic sufficient package.

cases.construction: Let A on l2(N) satisfy A e_(2k-1)=-e_(2k-1), A e_(2k)=e_(2k), so sigma(A)={-1,1}. Let L_n=span{e_1,...,e_(2n-2), v_n} with v_n=(e_(2n-1)+e_(2n))/sqrt(2). The union of L_n is dense. Since A v_n=(-e_(2n-1)+e_(2n))/sqrt(2) is orthogonal to L_n, the Galerkin compression P_Ln A|_Ln has eigenvalue 0 for every n, although 0 notin sigma(A).
cases.conclusion: Finite-dimensional self-adjoint compressions can exhibit persistent spectral pollution in a true spectral gap.
cases.limitation: This is a hostile calibration for projection-style convergence packages, not evidence that a specific Weil-form approximation pollutes.

cases.construction: For positive integers N,lambda let A_(N,lambda) be the one-dimensional self-adjoint operator with eigenvalue N/(N+lambda). Then lim_(lambda->infty) lim_(N->infty) A_(N,lambda)=1, while lim_(N->infty) lim_(lambda->infty) A_(N,lambda)=0, and along N=lambda the value is 1/2.
cases.conclusion: A two-parameter approximating family has no canonical global limit without a specified cofinal net/path or a uniform theorem proving path independence.
cases.limitation: The example is structural only; it does not prove N/lambda noncommutation in the RH source family.

cases.construction: Let G_n(z)=exp(n z) product_{k=1}^n (1-z^2/k^2). Every zero is real and the zeros +/-1,...,+/-n exactly match an increasing prefix of sin(pi z)/(pi z); also G_n(0)=1 for all n. But at z=1/2, product_{k=1}^n(1-1/(4k^2)) tends to 2/pi while exp(n/2) diverges, so G_n does not converge locally uniformly to sin(pi z)/(pi z).
cases.conclusion: Arbitrarily long exact finite zero-prefix agreement, real-rootedness, and a one-point normalization do not determine the target entire-function limit.
cases.limitation: A stronger source-side normalization/growth theorem could eliminate this pathology; that is precisely an RH-SPEC-002 obligation.

package_classification.reason: Hurwitz/Rouche transport excludes nonreal zeros and controls multiplicity once exact nonzero Xi local-uniform convergence and finite-stage real-rootedness are independently established.

Stronger operator topology plus compactness/no-pollution and an independent determinant/trace identity may transport isolated spectrum, but the required hypotheses have not been proved for the RH approximants.
Exact strong-resolvent examples allow approximant eigenvalues to disappear; generic self-adjoint projection approximations can pollute gaps.
Exact finite zero-prefix agreement can coexist with complete failure of local-uniform entire-function convergence.
Two-parameter self-adjoint families can have incompatible iterated and diagonal limits.

research_decision.question: For the source-defined finite/restricted RH approximants, what source-side uniform bounds and canonical normalization would imply local-uniform convergence of normalized entire determinants to Xi on every compact subset, or else decisively show that this determinant route cannot close?
research_decision.why: The calibration proves that generic strong-resolvent language, finite-prefix agreement, and unspecified joint limits are inadequate. Local-uniform entire-function convergence is the cleanest target-side sufficient package, so the next information bottleneck is source-side derivation of that convergence and normalization.
